sections.text:
This procedure details the steps required to completely check
the proper operation and calibration of the 7SA511 distance relay. It is
recommended this procedure be carried out on a yearly bases. This work be
carried out section of this document is divided into 3 sections.

The first preliminary steps to prepare for relay testing
describes the activities required prior to testing. Some of these steps could be
performed days before the actual test. The second section Preparation for
testing describes the steps to set up the equipment for performing the actual
tests. The third section is the actual test.

The document is formatted the way to minimize the possibility
of error causing personal injury or damage to equipment.

The first draft initialed 
& tested by eng. Abdel Azeez Mohamed at 29 Dec 1997 at Network training 
center.

Personal protective equipment must be used as safety shoes, and safety 
 Helmet.
Ensure that Line isolation is done.

Make sure CT secondary circuits are shorted and VT secondary circuits are opened before 
 injection.

sections.text: Preliminary Steps to Prepare for Relay Testing

items: Review technical references material Manufacturers manual.

Obtain copy of relay setting from field maintenance file and compare it
 with the setting on the relay.
Obtain outage for line protected by this relay.
Check that the bus and line disconnect switches are open and tagged.

Inspect the CT secondary circuits, the VT Miniature circuit breakers (MCBS),
 and all cables supplying the relay.

Use the 
 station drawings to isolate the following items
Breaker trip coils.
Breaker failure scheme associated with this relay.
Disturbance alarms and fault recorder associated with this relay.

sections.text: Testing the Relay and Protection Outputs

items:
Carefully follow all test procedure 
 steps.

Verify the test results match the relay setting, if not consult technical
 services.
Test trip the breaker associated with the relay.

Prior to Starting Testing Procedure (s) Ensure the Following
 Steps

items: This procedure is used to perform off load relay testing.

Look at the EEC panel nameplate and check that this EEC system designation
 agrees with the line that has been taken out of service for maintenance.
Check there is no AC current from CTs by using a clip on ammeter.
Check there is no AC voltage from VTs by using a voltmeter.
Connect the two units of the tester together.
Connect the tester to a 3 phase 380v power source.

Check the phase sequence by pressing push-buttons (I) ON for current
 tester unit, if the green lamp lights up, the phase sequence is correct, if
 the red one lights, the phase sequence is NOT correct and must be changed.
Connect the current circuit between the relay and the tester 7VP4800.
Connect the voltage circuit between the relay and the tester 7VP4900

Connect a free contact from the relay to the current unit 7VP4800. (Relay
 terminals (95, 96) to tester terminals (21, 22), as shown in figure (1)

items:
To test first step, block the time steps for all other zones
 (except first zone) and other function (by computer or keyboard on the
 relay).

Calculate the operating voltage corresponding to each angle from 0 to 90
 degrees for all the four zones tests as follows:

Press the push-button IL1 and In on current unit 7VP4800 to test
 phase R-N.
Adjust the voltage knob to maximum level.

Set the current selecting switch (S10) to the rated current of relay (1A
 or 5A)

Inject current by pressing the first push-button and rotating the knob IL1
 until the ammeter reads two times rated current (2*In).
Adjust the test angle to zero degrees.

Decrease the voltage by rotating the voltage knob counter-clockwise until
 the relay operates.
Record this value on the Test Sheet 1.

Compare this value (practical value) with (theoretical value), which was
 calculated, if the result is within 
 10%, it is acceptable, otherwise, consult technical services.

Repeat the above test from step 1 to step 8 but change the test angle to
 90 degrees.
Repeat the above test from step 1 to step 9 for phases S-N and T-N.

Press the push-buttons IL1 and IL2 on the current unit 7VP4800
 to test phaseR-S.
Adjust the voltage rotating knob to maximum level.
Put switch (S15) on L1 on unit 7VP4800.
Put switch (S6) on (L1-L2) on unit 7VP49.

Inject current by pressing push-buttons 1LI and 1L2 on unit 7VP4800 and
 rotate knobs1L1 and 1L2 until double rated current 2In is reached.
Adjust the test angle to zero degrees.

Decrease the voltage by rotating the voltage knob counterclockwise until
 the relay operates.
Record this value of voltage on Test Sheet 1.

Compare this 
 value (practical value) with (theoretical value), which was calculated.

If the result is within 10%, it is
 acceptable, otherwise, consult technical services.

Repeat the above test from step 1 to step 10 but change the test angle to
 90 degrees.
Repeat the above test from step 1 to step 11 for phases S-T and T-R

sections.text: Return Relay and Associated Equipment to Service

items:
Return relay to service by removing the test leads from the relay terminals
 block and the test set.
Make sure CT and VT secondary circuits are in normal condition.
Breaker trip coils.
Breaker failure scheme associated this relay.
Disturbance alarm and fault recorder associated with this relay.

sections.text: Request Power Line be returned to Service

items:
Take crossed reading of all AC currents and voltages supplied to the relay
 and compare them to those for normal load condition.

Check that readings agree with station meters (MW/MVAR/Power
 factor/Ampere/Voltages).
Place a copy of the test results in the field maintenance file.
